Fit a geographically weighted regression

Source: R/gwr-fit.R
ef_gwr_fit.Rd

Fits a geographically weighted regression (GWR) of a station variable on covariates for a given bandwidth: one weighted least squares (WLS) fit per station, with the hat statistics, leave-one-out (LOO) residuals, AICc, CV and the global (OLS) reference with the same design. This is the internal numeric core of the spatial regionalization: inputs are plain vectors and matrices in a projected coordinate reference system (metres); no raster object is involved.

The local estimator at regression point \(i\) is $$\hat\beta_i = (X^\top W_i X)^{-1} X^\top W_i y, \qquad \hat y_i = x_i^\top \hat\beta_i,$$ with \(W_i = \mathrm{diag}(w(d_{ij}/b_i))\). Row \(i\) of the hat matrix is \(s_i = x_i^\top (X^\top W_i X)^{-1} X^\top W_i\); the effective number of parameters is \(\mathrm{tr}(S)\).

Usage

ef_gwr_fit(
  y,
  x,
  coords,
  bandwidth,
  kernel,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  min_neighbours = NULL,
  scale_covariates = TRUE,
  station_id = NULL
)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector: the response at each station, in the unit of the variable (e.g. degC for air temperature).

x

Numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) with one row per station and one column per covariate, with unique column names (e.g. elevation [m]). The intercept is added internally.

coords

Numeric matrix with two columns: projected coordinates (x, y) of the stations [m]. Distances are Euclidean in this CRS (decision GW-09); geographic coordinates (degrees) must be projected first.

bandwidth

Either a number, the fixed bandwidth [m] (when adaptive = FALSE) or the number of neighbours k, a whole number in [1, n] (when adaptive = TRUE); or an earthflux_gwr_bandwidth object returned by ef_gwr_bandwidth(), whose kernel, bandwidth type, neighbour rule, profile and flags are then carried to the fit.

kernel

Character, no default (decision GW-04 is open): one of "gaussian", "exponential", "bisquare", "tricube", "boxcar". May be omitted when bandwidth is an earthflux_gwr_bandwidth object; if given it must match the object.

adaptive

Logical. FALSE for a fixed bandwidth in metres, TRUE for an adaptive bandwidth given as k nearest stations (the k-th smallest distance, counting the regression point itself when it is a station). Taken from bandwidth when that is an earthflux_gwr_bandwidth object and adaptive is not supplied.

min_neighbours

NULL or a whole number: minimum number of neighbours of a regression point (stations with a non-zero weight for compact kernels; stations within one bandwidth for the gaussian and exponential kernels). NULL uses the mathematical minimum p + 1 (p coefficients for the local fit plus one so that the LOO fit stays identifiable; decision GW-06). Larger values are accepted but should be justified by a reference; they are recorded in config.

scale_covariates

Logical. Whether to centre and scale the covariates internally (by their mean and standard deviation over the stations of the fit) to condition the local systems. Coefficients are always reported in original units and predictions do not change.

station_id

NULL or a vector of unique station identifiers. By default names(y), rownames(x) or the row numbers.

Value

An object of class c("earthflux_gwr", "earthflux_regionalization", "list") with elements:

  • call; variable, target_time, unit: NULL (set by the regionalization orchestrator);

  • stations: data frame with one row per input station: station_id, x, y (coordinates [m]), the covariates, observed, fitted, residual, loo_fitted, loo_residual, s_ii, local_r2, bandwidth_i [m], n_nonzero, kappa, rank_ok, status ("used" or "excluded") and exclusion_reason;

  • coefficients: matrix (stations used x p) of local coefficients in original units ((Intercept) in the unit of y, slopes in unit of y per unit of each covariate);

  • kernel; bandwidth: list(type, value, unit, selected_by);

  • conventions: the conventions applied (k including the point itself, boxcar support d <= b, AICc definition, sigma, local R2, LOO, distance method, covariate scaling, numerical tolerances);

  • fit: n, p, rss, sigma_ml = sqrt(RSS/n), sigma_edf = sqrt(RSS/edf), enp = tr(S), tr_sts = tr(S'S), enp_alt = 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S), edf = n - 2 tr(S) + tr(S'S), aicc, aic (uncorrected, report only), cv, rmse_loo and r2 (global, 1 - RSS/TSS);

  • global_reference: OLS with the same design (coefficients, rss, enp = p, aicc, cv);

  • profile, search: from the bandwidth selection, NULL when the bandwidth is given by the user;

  • flags: list of earthflux_flag records (object and station scope);

  • config: covariates, their units (attribute "units" of x, if any), min_neighbours and its source, scaling;

  • model: what ef_gwr_predict() needs (stations used, response, covariates, coordinates, scaling, covariate range and convex hull);

  • provenance: method, package and R versions, flags_evaluated.

Details

Stations with missing values. A station with a missing response, covariate or coordinate is excluded with its reason in stations and the flag EF_GWR_STATION_EXCLUDED; nothing is removed silently. Infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error.

Errors. n < p + 3 stations with complete data: earthflux_gwr_insufficient_stations (fields n, p). A local design of deficient rank at a station (e.g. only the station itself has a non-zero weight): earthflux_gwr_singular_error (field stations). A covariate constant among the stations, or stations with identical coordinates and covariates: earthflux_input_error. Inconsistent dimensions: earthflux_input_error (the spec's earthflux_dimension_error is not a separate class; dimension errors are input errors as in the rest of the core). Unknown kernel: earthflux_unknown_method. Fixed bandwidth not positive, or k outside [1, n] or not whole: earthflux_domain_error. All earthflux_gwr_* errors inherit earthflux_gwr_error.

Flags. EF_GWR_STATION_EXCLUDED (record), EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS (record: stations with fewer than min_neighbours neighbours; their LOO residual is NA when the fit interpolates them), EF_GWR_AICC_UNDEFINED (object: n - 2 - tr(S) <= 0, AICc is NA), plus the object flags of the bandwidth selection when bandwidth is an earthflux_gwr_bandwidth object.

Kernels and conventions

With \(r = d/b_i\): gaussian \(\exp(-r^2/2)\), exponential \(\exp(-r)\), bisquare \((1-r^2)^2\) for \(d < b_i\), tricube \((1-r^3)^3\) for \(d < b_i\), boxcar 1 for \(d \le b_i\); 0 otherwise. The boxcar support \(d \le b\) (decision GW-03) differs from the strict inequality of Table 1 of Gollini et al. (2015) and matches GWmodel 2.4-1. With an adaptive bandwidth and the bisquare or tricube kernel, the station at distance exactly \(b_i\) has weight 0, so at most k - 1 stations (including the point itself) have a non-zero weight.

Verification status

Local estimator and kernels: VERIFICADA as content of Gollini et al. (2015; preprint arXiv:1306.0413v2, section 6.1 and Table 1); as EarthFlux definitions CANDIDATA (corroborada): reproduced to 1e-10 relative by GWmodel 2.4-1 in the cross-check tests. The k convention and the boxcar boundary are EarthFlux conventions (GW-03). AICc: see ef_gwr_bandwidth(). Local R2 (weighted mean of the local fit, GW-13), tr(S'S), 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S), edf and the condition number: CANDIDATA. Original attributions (Brunsdon et al., 1996; Fotheringham et al., 2002) not read.

References

Gollini, I., Lu, B., Charlton, M., Brunsdon, C., & Harris, P. (2015). GWmodel: An R package for exploring spatial heterogeneity using geographically weighted models. Journal of Statistical Software, 63(17). doi:10.18637/jss.v063.i17

Brunsdon, C., Fotheringham, A. S., & Charlton, M. E. (1996). Geographically weighted regression: A method for exploring spatial nonstationarity. Geographical Analysis, 28(4), 281-298. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1996.tb00936.x

See also

ef_gwr_bandwidth() to select the bandwidth, ef_gwr_predict() to predict at new locations, ef_gwr_diagnostics().

Examples

# Six stations (projected coordinates in m), air temperature (degC) and
# elevation (m)
coords <- cbind(c(0, 10000, 0, 10000, 20000, 30000),
                c(0, 0, 10000, 10000, 0, 30000))
elev <- cbind(elevation = c(100, 300, 500, 200, 800, 1200))
ta <- c(20.0, 18.9, 17.5, 19.6, 15.4, 13.1)
fit <- ef_gwr_fit(ta, elev, coords, bandwidth = 20000,
                  kernel = "gaussian")
fit
#> <earthflux_gwr>
#> Method: gwr; kernel: gaussian; bandwidth (fixed): 20000 m; selected by: user
#> Stations: 6 used, 0 excluded; p = 2 coefficients
#> tr(S) = 2.7382; 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S) = 3.1810; RSS = 0.0548862; RMSE_LOO = 0.241379
#> AICc: GWR 24.412005, global OLS 9.309406; CV: GWR 0.349583, global OLS 0.254309
#> Flags (warning): EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS [1/6]
#> Conventions: k includes the point itself; AICc with ML sigma and tr(S)
fit$coefficients
#>   (Intercept)    elevation
#> 1    20.78793 -0.006583592
#> 2    20.79976 -0.006599539
#> 3    20.78418 -0.006545054
#> 4    20.79070 -0.006545003
#> 5    20.80460 -0.006598231
#> 6    20.77549 -0.006430294
